transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. How can I help you today?

Um, yeah… thanks for seeing me. I guess I’m here because my work physical kind of flagged something. The doctor there said my weight was too low and thought I should talk to someone.

I mean, I don’t feel bad, really. If anything I feel a little lighter on my feet when I play basketball, and at the garage I don’t feel as weighed down moving around all day. So I wasn’t really thinking it was a big problem, but… I figured I should follow up like they asked.
Have you been trying to lose weight or change your eating habits on purpose, or are you eating the same amount as before?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m on a diet exactly. It’s more like I’ve just gotten used to keeping things pretty simple. Most days I’ll have coffee in the morning, and then maybe later a small sandwich or, you know, half of whatever’s around.

With the shop running late a lot and the house being busy, it just feels easier if I stick to my own rules. I know that might sound a little… strict, but it feels manageable to me. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you restrict your eating because you’re concerned about gaining weight or because you see yourself as overweight, even if others might not see you that way?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I look overweight exactly. But yeah, I guess if the scale goes up even a pound, or my jeans feel a little tighter, I start thinking I’m getting kind of soft.

It’s probably silly, but I worry I’ll be slower at work moving around cars, or not as quick running up and down the court. So I do try to keep it from creeping up, if that makes sense.
Do you push yourself to exercise more or harder if you feel like you've eaten too much or gained a little weight?

Um… I don’t know if I’d put it that way. I mean, I like staying active, and basketball’s kind of my outlet after work, so if I’ve had a heavier meal I might feel like I should move around a bit more.

But I’m not, like… punishing myself or anything. At least I don’t think so. I just feel better if I’ve gotten some exercise in, if that makes sense. Is that… is that what you’re asking?
Have you ever made yourself vomit or used laxatives, diet pills, or anything like that to try to control your weight or shape?

No… I don’t do that. I mean, I’ve never made myself throw up or taken pills or laxatives for it.

I mostly just try to be careful with what I eat and keep active. I know that still might sound a little controlled, but I’m not doing those kinds of things. Is that okay?
Do you ever feel intense anxiety or fear about gaining weight, even a small amount, or go out of your way to avoid gaining weight in ways that might seem extreme to others?

Yeah… I mean, “intense” sounds kind of strong, but I do get pretty anxious if I notice the scale’s up even a pound, or if my jeans feel tighter.

I start thinking I’m getting soft, and then I worry I won’t be as quick at work moving around cars, or running up and down the court. So I guess I do try to keep it from going up. I don’t know if that counts as extreme, but it probably bothers me more than it should.
Do you see your body differently than others might, or do you feel that you need to lose more weight even if people around you might say you're already at a healthy or low weight?

I mean… I know some people are worried, yeah. My family’s mentioned it, and I get that they’re trying to help.

But honestly, I kind of feel like they’re making more out of it than it is. I’m still going to work, still getting things done around the house, still playing ball on weekends… so in my head it’s like, if I can do all that, I can’t be doing that bad, right?

I’m not trying to be difficult. I just don’t always see what they’re seeing, I guess.

Have these habits around eating and exercise started to interfere with your life—like making it hard to focus at work, affecting your relationships, or causing physical problems like dizziness or fatigue?

Not too much with work, I don’t think. I’m still showing up at the garage and getting through the day, and I still play in my basketball league, so I wouldn’t say it’s ruining things or anything.

But… yeah, at home it’s caused some friction. I’ll kind of avoid sitting down for regular family meals, or I’ll make an excuse, and then people start asking if I’m okay. I know they mean well, but it turns into a thing sometimes. I guess that part has been harder on everybody than I want to admit. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you judge yourself or feel that your value as a person depends on your weight, shape, or how you look?

I don’t know if I’d say my value as a person depends on it… that sounds pretty heavy.

I mean, I do feel better about myself when I feel like I’m in shape or my clothes fit right. If I feel like I look bad, it can get in my head some. But I still know I’m a good worker, a decent dad, all that. At least, I think so.

Maybe I put more on it than I should, but I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. Is that kind of what you’re asking?
Do you find that your thoughts about your weight or shape have a big impact on how you feel about yourself overall?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, it affects my mood some, yeah… like if I feel like I’m not looking right, I can get kind of down on myself or irritated.

But I don’t think it’s everything, if that makes sense. I still care about being a good dad, doing my job right, being reliable. So I wouldn’t want to say my whole self-worth is wrapped up in it.

Maybe it has more of an effect than I like to admit, though. I don’t know if that’s answering it the right way.
When you look in the mirror, do you feel like you still appear overweight to yourself, even if others might say you look thin or underweight?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t really say I look overweight, exactly. That feels like too strong a word.

Sometimes I look in the mirror and think there are spots that don’t look right, or I don’t look as lean as I’d like, but if someone said I looked thin, I guess I can understand that too. I’m not trying to argue with them.

Maybe I’m just harder on myself than other people are. Is that what you mean?
Do you feel like your weight or body shape is significantly different from what you see in the mirror, or do you worry about parts of your body in a way that doesn't match what others might see?

I’m not sure I’d say it’s “significantly different,” no. Like, I don’t look in the mirror and think I’m seeing a totally different person or anything.

I guess there are certain areas I notice more than other people probably would… and I can get stuck on them a little. But I also know people may not see it the same way I do. I’m trying not to make it sound dramatic, because I don’t know if it really is.

Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Has worrying about your weight or shape ever caused you to feel so distressed that it affected your ability to function normally, like making it hard for you to interact with others, go to work, or enjoy activities you used to like?

Not to the point where I’m missing work or anything like that. I’m still showing up at the garage, getting my jobs done, and I’m still playing in my basketball league, so I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.

I guess where it does cause problems is more at home. I’ve been avoiding sitting down for regular family meals sometimes, and that’s… caused some tension. People keep asking if I’m okay, and I usually just say I’m fine, but I can tell it bothers them.

So, yeah, it affects things some. I’m not sure if that counts as “functioning” being affected, but that’s probably the honest answer.

Do you feel that your concerns about weight or shape cause you significant distress or interfere with your ability to fully participate in your life, such as affecting your relationships, enjoyment of activities, or your emotional well-being?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to say it’s taking over my whole life or anything. I’m still going to work at the garage, still getting through the day, and I’m still playing basketball, so in that sense I’m functioning.

But it does affect things at home more than I’d like to admit. I’ll avoid sitting down for regular family meals sometimes, and that’s caused tension. People notice and ask if I’m okay, and then I just kind of say I’m fine, even if it’s awkward.

So… yeah, I guess it does interfere some, mostly with family stuff and feeling comfortable. I’m not sure if that’s what you’d call significant, but it’s there.
Would you say that how you see your weight or shape has a strong impact on how you feel about yourself overall, or do you feel like it's just a smaller part of how you see yourself?

I think it’s… probably a smaller part? I don’t really want to say my whole self-worth is wrapped up in that, because I don’t think that’s true.

I mean, if I’m feeling uncomfortable about my body, it can put me in a bad mood or make me kind of self-conscious, but I still see myself as a dad, husband, mechanic, teammate… all that stuff. So it matters, yeah, but I don’t know that it defines me.

Does that answer it the right way?
Can you describe how much these concerns about your weight or shape bother you emotionally, and do they interfere with your ability to enjoy life or do the things you need to do each day?

It bothers me some, yeah… emotionally I get uncomfortable and kind of tense about it, but I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t function.

I’m still going to the garage, getting my work done, and I’m still playing in my basketball league, so day-to-day I’m managing. The main place it gets in the way is at home. I’ve been avoiding sitting down for regular family meals sometimes, and that’s caused some tension. People notice and ask if I’m okay, and I usually just brush it off.

So… it does interfere a bit, mostly with family stuff and enjoying being comfortable around meals. I don’t know if that’s the kind of answer you’re looking for, but that’s probably the honest version.
Can you tell me if, and how often, your concerns about weight or shape make it hard for you to be around friends or family, especially during meals or other times when food is involved?

Yeah… I mean, it’s not like I’m avoiding everybody all the time. I’m still going to work at the garage and I still play in my basketball league, so I’m not totally shut down or anything.

But with family meals, yeah, that’s where it comes up more. I’ll sometimes avoid sitting down for a regular meal at home, or kind of make excuses, and then people notice. They’ll ask if I’m okay, and it gets tense or awkward.

So… not every single time, but often enough that it’s caused some tension at home. I guess that counts as interfering, right?
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see a body that others might describe as thin or underweight, or do you still see yourself as heavier than you actually are?

I mean… I know people say I look too thin, or they act worried when they see me, but when I look in the mirror it doesn’t really hit me that way.

I guess I figure maybe they’re making a bigger deal out of it than it is, because I’m still going to work, still handling stuff at home, still playing ball on weekends. So in my head it’s like… if I can do all that, I can’t be that bad, right?

I’m not trying to argue with anyone. That’s just kind of how I see it. Does that make sense?
Do you believe that your current weight is too low or that you might be underweight, or do you feel that your weight is fine or even too high despite what others might say?

I guess… I don’t really see it as too low, if I’m being honest. I know people are worried and they’ll say I look like I’ve lost too much, but part of me thinks they’re maybe making more of it than it is.

I mean, I’m still showing up to work, doing what I need to do at home, and playing ball on weekends, so it’s hard for me to think it’s that serious. Maybe that sounds like I’m brushing it off… I’m not trying to. That’s just where my head goes with it.

Can you tell me if your concerns about weight or shape involve behaviors or feelings that don’t quite fit into a clear pattern, or if they seem mixed with other issues that might not be typical of a specific eating disorder?

I’m not sure I totally know how to separate that out, honestly.

It mostly just feels like the same stuff I’ve been saying — worrying about how I look or what I’m eating, and then trying not to make a big scene about it. I don’t know if there’s some other issue mixed in or if it’s supposed to fit a certain pattern.

I guess I haven’t really thought of it that way. If that makes sense.
